Inventory of /home/c.dumas/claude-projects/sarcasm-persona-exploration/article/ — a Quarto website project with three report versions (v1_report.qmd, v2_report.qmd, index.qmd = de facto v3/latest) sharing one _quarto.yml and custom.css. All narrative charts are generated live in Python code cells (plotly), not pre-rendered images, except two static PNGs embedded in index.qmd. A rendered but source-deleted v3_report.html/.quarto cache confirms index.qmd was formerly named v3_report.qmd (byte-identical rendered output to index.html). SCOPE NOTE: task explicitly listed index.qmd, v1_report.qmd, v2_report.qmd, _quarto.yml, custom.css — that's what's inventoried below. v3_report.qmd itself does not exist on disk (only its stale render/cache does); confirmed via byte-identical file size to index.html so no separate content was lost from this inventory. === SITE-WIDE / SHARED (_quarto.yml + custom.css) === _quarto.yml: `project.type: website`, single global `website.title`, no navbar/sidebar items configured — Quarto's default page chrome only (floating right-margin TOC, no cross-page nav links). `format.html`: theme cosmo (light only, no dark-mode alt theme), toc:true, toc-depth:3, code-fold:true, css: custom.css. jupyter: python3 declared at site level (index.qmd/v2 redeclare it in their own front matter; v1 does not, relying on the site default). custom.css (23 rule blocks, ~90 lines) defines: `.sample-box` (bordered card, max-height:150px collapsed, gradient fade-out footer reading "click to expand", `.expanded` class removes the cap, `.short-text` suppresses the fade for already-short content) + 7 left-border accent variants (`.sample-base/.sample-full/.sample-early/.sample-middle/.sample-late/.sample-amp-low/.sample-amp-high`, each a different color) + `.sample-label`; `.evidence` badge (4 color variants: strong-for/moderate-for/suggestive/against); `.model-llama/.model-gemma/.model-qwen` colored+bold inline text spans; `.comparison-table` (bordered/striped table style); `.score-high/.score-mid/.score-low` inline score badges. NOTE: `.comparison-table` and the three `.score-*` classes are defined but never referenced by any class-attribute in any of the three .qmd files (dead/orphaned CSS) — grepped, zero hits. === FEATURES BY CATEGORY === 1. [chart] Layer-range sarcasm line/bar chart (hero finding). Plotly (go.Figure, Scatter in index.qmd/lines+markers; Bar in v1/v2), one trace per model (llama/gemma/qwen), x=layer range (base/0-20/.../full), y=sarcasm 0-10. Hover shows exact value + n (index/v2 via customdata); asymmetric error bars = 95% bootstrap CI (index/v2 only, computed via a local `bootstrap_ci()` helper, 1000 resamples, seeded in index.qmd (`np.random.default_rng(42)`) but unseeded in v2). No baseline reference line. v1's version is a grouped bar chart (2 models only: llama/gemma) with data-labels-outside, no CI/error bars, no hover customization. Locations: index.qmd:105-141 (Finding 1), v2_report.qmd:114-152 ("Hero Finding"), v1_report.qmd:96-125 (Phase 1 section). 2. [chart] Per-prompt disaggregation line chart (consistency check). Plotly subplots, 1 row × 3 (or 2) cols, one panel per model, one colored line per individual prompt (Set3 palette), shows the same layer-range pattern holds prompt-by-prompt (no single outlier prompt driving it). Always inside a collapsed callout. Locations: index.qmd:173-198 (`callout-tip collapse="true"`, "Per-prompt consistency check"), v2_report.qmd:166-194 (`callout-tip collapse="true"`, "Per-prompt breakdown"), v1_report.qmd:136-152 (`callout-note collapse="true"`, "Per-prompt breakdown (Phase 1)" — px.bar grouped by config instead of a line chart) + v1_report.qmd:355-374 (Phase-2 fine-grained per-prompt variant) + v1 amplification/boundary per-prompt variants (below). 3. Counts: v1 has 8 such collapsed callouts, v2 has 3, index has 3 (plus the top-level, non-collapsed "Judging methodology note" callout in v2:105-109 which is NOT collapsed by default — inconsistent with the others). 25. [layout] Wide breakout containers: `{.column-page}` (full-bleed width, used for most charts + all curated sample-card blocks + both static PNGs) and the narrower `{.column-body-outset}` (used once, for the correlation-heatmap chart only, v2_report.qmd:235). index.qmd and v1_report.qmd use `.column-page` exclusively wherever a breakout is applied. 26. [layout] Right-margin floating Table of Contents (`toc: true`, `toc-depth: 3`), Quarto default — auto-generated from H2/H3 headings, active-section highlighting via scrollspy (`nav-link active` class swap confirmed in rendered index.html). Same in all three reports (own front-matter `toc: true` in each, redundant with the site-level default in _quarto.yml). 27. [layout] `code-fold: true` — every Python code cell is collapsed by default behind a "Code" toggle in the rendered HTML, site-wide (_quarto.yml + repeated per-file front matter). 28. [stat-display] Inline hover "n=" sample-count annotations on chart tooltips (not a standalone stat tile — embedded in chart hover templates via `customdata`). Present on: chart #1 (index/v2), chart #4 (index/v2), chart #15's per-line n labels via `text=[f"n={int(n)}" for n in ...]` (index.qmd:436,444). Not present in v1's charts (v1 has no hover n= anywhere; v1 states sample counts only in prose, e.g. "n=9 per condition", "189 Phase 1, 366 Phase 2 samples"). 29. [stat-display] Live filtered-count line above the Sample Explorer card list: `N samples matching filters`, recomputed reactively as filters change. Location: index.qmd:605 (own OJS cell) and v2_report.qmd:460 (separate OJS cell from the card-rendering cell, unlike index.qmd which combines count+cards in a single cell). Not present in v1 (v1 shows `md\`Showing ${shuffled.length} of ${filtered.length} samples:\`` instead — same information, different phrasing/placement, v1_report.qmd:1009). 30. [data-plumbing] Direct pandas CSV/parquet loading in the top Python setup cell, per report: v1 loads 9 separate CSVs (`data/phase1_layer_scores.csv`, `phase1_by_prompt.csv`, `phase2_fine_grained.csv`, `phase2_by_prompt.csv`, `qwen_combos.csv`, `amplification.csv`, `amplification_by_prompt.csv`, `layer_amp_combos.csv`, `prompt_boundaries.csv`, `samples.csv`) — no parquet at all. v2/index switch to 3 parquet files as the primary source (`v2_judgments.parquet`, `v2_aggregated.parquet`, `v2_by_prompt.parquet`) plus a mix of leftover CSVs for sections carried over from Phase 1/2 (`v2_dimension_correlations.csv`, `phase2_fine_grained.csv`, `qwen_combos.csv`, `amplification.csv`, `prompt_boundaries.csv`; index.qmd additionally loads `bestslice_boundaries.csv` and `layer_amp_combos.csv` inline inside their respective chart cells rather than the setup cell). No DuckDB/OJS-SQL anywhere in any of the 3 reports. 31. [data-plumbing] OJS/JS data handoff — two distinct, non-interchangeable mechanisms across versions. v1: OJS cell calls `FileAttachment("data/samples.csv").csv({typed:true})`, i.e. the browser makes a runtime fetch for a standalone CSV copied into `_site/data/samples.csv` at render time. v2/index: the Python setup cell calls `ojs_define(samples=json.loads(_ojs_df.fillna("").to_json(orient="records")), model_labels=MODEL_LABELS, dim_list=DIMS)` — data is serialized to JSON and embedded inline in the rendered HTML (`application/json` script blocks with `ojs-define` ids, confirmed via grep on the rendered _site/index.html), no separate network fetch. Category dtype columns are cast to str before serialization to avoid JSON errors (index.qmd:76-77 / v2_report.qmd:84-85, identical snippet). 32. [data-plumbing] Custom Python helper functions redefined near-identically in each report's setup cell rather than imported from a shared module: `raw_html()` (HTML display passthrough), `escape_html()` (html.escape + newline→`
`, defined but never called downstream in any of the 3 files — dead code all 3 places), `bootstrap_ci()` (1000-resample bootstrap mean CI). v1 has none of these three helpers (v1 predates the CI/raw-html features). index.qmd's `bootstrap_ci` seeds `np.random.default_rng(42)`; v2's identical-looking function uses unseeded `np.random.choice` — a reproducibility inconsistency between the two despite v2 predating index and index visually building on v2's code. 33. [styling-theming] Shared `custom.css` (see site-wide section above) linked via front-matter `css: custom.css` in all 3 reports individually (plus once at the site level in _quarto.yml — quadruple-declared). Quarto `cosmo` Bootswatch theme for all chrome (fonts, nav, callout boxes); no dark-mode variant, no custom font-face, no OS dark-mode media query anywhere in custom.css. 34. [styling-theming] Inline colored `` text highlighting for model names in prose (v1_report.qmd:467, 777-779 only) — not used at all in v2 or index (both use plain text model names in prose, relying on chart-legend color alone for the color-coding). 35. [other] Footnote-style caveat using Pandoc's `^[...]` inline-footnote syntax, rendered as a numbered footnote with hover/click reveal at the bottom of page. Location: v1_report.qmd:471 (Qwen's amplification 1x-baseline approximation caveat). Not used in v2/index — the same caveat is instead stated as plain prose (index.qmd doesn't mention the approximation caveat at all in the amplification section — appears to have been dropped/forgotten across versions, though the Limitations section of index.qmd:558-564 does list other caveats). 36. [other] Appendix judging-rubric block: v1 shows the FULL literal Haiku prompt/rubric text in a fenced plain-code block (v1_report.qmd:878-892, all 5 dimension anchors 0/10 spelled out). v2's Appendix instead just references an external file path (`experiments/exp_001_phase1_replication/rejudge_qwen/judging/criteria.md`) without reproducing it (v2_report.qmd:494) — a regression in self-containedness. index.qmd has no Appendix / judging-criteria section at all (dropped entirely; the info survives only as a one-line bullet in the Setup section, index.qmd:99). 37. ["other] "Prompts used" appendix listing (creative/direct/instruction categories with example titles) as a collapsed callout. Location: v2_report.qmd:497-505 only. v1 states the same prompt categories in prose in its Setup section (no dedicated list); index.qmd states it as a one-line bullet in Setup (index.qmd:98) with no dedicated appendix section.

report:
Feature Inventory — negative_scaling_exp/article/

Six Quarto reports share one site (_quarto.yml, custom.css) documenting a LoRA-adapter-negation study. Two major implementation eras coexist: an earlier Python/Plotly-driven style (index.qmd, v2_report.qmd, safety_report.qmd) and a later OJS/DuckDB-reactive style (v3_report.qmd, v3_1_data.qmd), with v3_report_my_version.qmd an explicit alternate (Python-static) rendering of the same v3 content, ending in a bolted-on OJS explorer. Recurring features are listed once with every location; one-offs are listed under their single location. Full detail is in the `features` array; this text summarizes the architecture found.

Site-wide: navbar linking 5 pages, site TOC, built-in Quarto search, code-fold collapsed source cells, cosmo Bootstrap theme (no dark mode), several custom.css classes for sample cards/badges — some of which (.evidence.*, .cond-*, .wide-table) are defined but never actually referenced by any .qmd (dead CSS).

Charts: three distinct Python-side implementations of a "coherence threshold slider" (precomputed-traces/visibility-toggle in index.qmd; full-restyle-rebuild in safety_report.qmd; y-only restyle in v2_report.qmd), plus a completely different OJS-reactive architecture in v3_report.qmd/v3_1_data.qmd where a single global fixed-position slider (`viewof minCoherence`) drives live client-side d3.rollup aggregation and Plotly.newPlot re-renders, with Wilson-score binomial CI error bars computed both in Python and OJS. safety_report.qmd additionally has a unique sticky top-of-page raw HTML/JS bar that syncs every chart's own slider simultaneously (the only true cross-chart sync). Chart types found: grouped/stacked bar, line dose-response with baseline/reference lines, stacked-area identity distribution, small-multiples facet grids (2x2 and 5x2), several heatmaps, a curated bubble/quadrant scatter with danger-zone shading, and a jittered 2D scattergl plot.

Filter-controls: two explorer architectures recur across the site — an in-memory JSON array filtered with OJS `.filter()` (index.qmd, safety_report.qmd) and a DuckDB-WASM + Parquet SQL-query explorer (v2_report.qmd, v3_report.qmd, v3_report_my_version.qmd, and three separate instances in v3_1_data.qmd for identity/safety/system-prompt data). Both pair dropdown/range filters with a "Draw Random Samples" button.

Sample-display: a Python `sample_html()`/`show_samples()` card renderer (reimplemented near-identically per file) and its OJS `htl.html` twin, both with click-to-expand/collapse for long text; a recurring "cherry-picked vs. random (not cherry-picked)" paired-section convention used ~10+ times to validate curated examples aren't unrepresentative; a categorized qualitative-sample bank (`samples_by_cat`/`show_category`) unique to the v3 reports.

Tables: mostly static markdown tables, plus one conditionally-row-colored HTML comparison table (index.qmd) and one output:asis-generated markdown table.

Data-plumbing: the two explorer backends above, a Python→OJS bridge (`ojs_define`) passing pre-stratified aggregates for reactive client-side recomputation, pre-built cherry-picked/random JSON sample banks, and a folder of 57 standalone pre-rendered Plotly HTML files (figures/) that are not referenced by any .qmd — orphaned analysis artifacts.

Stat-display: a small "dataset summary" info box with computed n-counts (v2/safety reports only), n= counts baked into every chart hovertemplate, and CI error bars functioning as an implicit uncertainty stat.

Notable structural observation: v3_report.qmd and v3_report_my_version.qmd are two different implementations (OJS-reactive vs. Python-static) of the same v3 analysis with nearly identical section headings, and v3_1_data.qmd functions as a long-tail reactive-chart appendix to v3_report.qmd rather than a standalone narrative.

Inventoried the two rendered pages of the Assistant-Axis × Character-Training report (index.qmd, 993 lines — main report; constitution.qmd, 762 lines — validation follow-up) plus their shared _quarto.yml project config and the two page-specific CSS files it references (custom.css, styles.css). Both .qmd sources were read in full rather than the rendered HTML (per the practical caution), since the source Quarto markup is authoritative and much smaller than the multi-MB rendered artifacts in _site/. I grepped the rendered _site/index.html only to confirm two behaviors invisible from source: the Quarto `website` project type auto-injects a search box in the navbar, and no dark-mode CSS exists anywhere in the stack.

Two adjacent files (qualitative_sarcasm.md, qualitative_misalignment.md, qualitative_goodness.md) sit in the same directory and have their own _site renders, but _quarto.yml's `render:` list only names index.qmd and constitution.qmd — they are not part of these two pages and were left out of scope per your file list.

Notable structural facts that shaped the inventory:
- The report runs two parallel, non-interoperating data paths on the same two parquet files: an OJS+DuckDB-WASM path (live, queryable, drives every filter/explorer) and a Python/pandas path (static, baked into HTML at render time via Plotly and raw_html()-injected cards). Nothing bridges them — e.g. a chart drawn in Python cannot see the OJS min-coherence slider's value.
- Three near-identical "renderDual" implementations exist: a 6-prompt version (index.qmd) and a CI-augmented version (constitution.qmd) are structurally the same function repeated with a small delta (error bars), which is exactly the kind of duplication a shared building block would collapse.
- A `.evidence`-class CSS block (strong/medium/suggestive/against evidence coding) is defined in custom.css but I verified via grep that it is never applied by any content in these two files — likely vestigial from a sibling report sharing the stylesheet.
- The whole report is fixed-light-mode: no `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block and no theme toggle, with chart/card colors hardcoded ad hoc as inline hex values rather than CSS custom properties, so nothing would adapt automatically if reused in a dark-aware harness.

## Scope and important caveat

Target file: `/home/c.dumas/projects2/weird-personas/external/negation_neglect/experiments_appendix/c2_base_model_vs_instruct/.draft_report.qmd` (253 lines, pure Quarto markdown — zero executable code cells: grepped for triple-backtick fences and `{python}`/`{r}`/`{ojs}` markers, 0 hits).

**This report's `format:` is `pdf` (lualatex), not `html`.** There is no OJS, no DuckDB, no inline JSON payload, no JS at all — every "chart" is a pre-rendered PNG (matplotlib) embedded via plain Markdown image syntax, and every "table" is a static Markdown table. Confirmed the actual render target is a PDF: `reports/c2_full_report_v3_20260521T194110Z.pdf` exists; no `.html` output anywhere in the subexperiment tree. Because of this, the interactivity attributes the categories ask about (hover tooltips, CI toggles, live filters) are structurally absent from *this* document — CIs and per-seed overlays are baked into the static images at generation time by an external Python script, not by the report itself. I've noted this per-feature rather than omitting the features, since the parent task is presumably deciding which of these need to be *newly built* as interactive HTML components (none of the interactivity exists yet to reuse) versus which layout/content patterns can be reused as-is.

The `.qmd` itself is not hand-authored per render either: it's fully string-templated by `scripts/render_report.sh` (and a `render_report_v3.sh` variant) from `results_aggregated.csv`, which also stages figures into a transient `figures/` directory next to the `.qmd` before calling Quarto (`cp -r "$FIG_DIR" "$REPORT_DIR/figures"` — this is why no `figures/` dir exists on disk now; the real PNGs live in `results_aggregated_figures/` and `results_aggregated_figures_v3/`). The YAML's `execute: {echo: false, warning: false}` is vestigial — there's nothing to execute.

### data-plumbing
- **Fully string-templated .qmd, no executable cells** — whole document is generated by `scripts/render_report.sh` from `results_aggregated.csv` (long-form: condition, seed, lr, backbone, lora_kind, category, metric, mean, ci_lo, ci_hi, n, source); markdown tables and prose numbers are templated as literal text, not computed in-document.
